title: CRYPTONITE: Scalable Accelerator Design for Cryptographic Primitives and Algorithms
authors: Maheswaran, Karthikeya Sharma; Bossut, Camille; Wanna, Andy; Zhang, Qirun; Hao, Cong
relevance_reason: Composes per-kernel Pareto designs (sum of resources, max latency): an instance of local composition relevant to joint-composition failure; no interaction measured.
research_problem: Straight-line (loop-free) C code of cryptographic primitives synthesizes via HLS into large, non-scalable hardware and offers no parameterizable constructs for HLS DSE; the paper seeks correct-by-construction restructuring that enables resource/latency trade-off exploration, including across multiple co-deployed primitives.
method: Two stages: (1) an e-graph (egg) loop synthesizer using equality saturation plus data-dependence analysis (SVF) and GiNaC-based pattern abstraction to re-roll straight-line code into loops/arrays with preserved equivalence; (2) a hardware implementation explorer that enumerates loop/pragma variants and uses an analytical QoR estimator (latency cycles and DSP) to prune to a Pareto front, with Pareto points fed back for further refinement.
benchmark: Fiat Cryptography primitives (paper states 12 primitive types tested); reported: Curve25519, P521, P448, Secp256k1, P384 multiplication and square kernels.
hardware_platform: Xilinx xczu9eg-ffvb1156-2-e (ZCU102-class Zynq UltraScale+) as synthesis target
metrics: Latency (cycles), DSP/LUT/FF/BRAM utilization, Normalized Performance Index (NPI, weighted normalized latency+resource), speedup
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: 'Cryptonite achieves scalable designs with up to 88.88% reduced resource usage and a 54.31% improvement in latency compared to naively synthesized designs'; single-kernel up to 2.75x speedup and 2.03x resource reduction; for a 3-kernel joint deployment DSP usage reduced ~62.21% and execution time by 27 cycles vs naive straight-line code.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on e-graph loop re-rolling; for Secp256k1 and P384 transformations increased latency due to loop-carried carry chains; QoR estimator only predicts latency and DSP analytically; no RTL/post-implementation comparison; ScaleHLS failed on several primitives.
gap_status: This paper does not report: interactions measured; decision or pareto stability; lifecycle or configuration cost. Not a novelty claim.

title: Exact and Heuristic Allocation of Multi-kernel Applications to Multi-FPGA Platforms
authors: Shan, Junnan; Casu, Mario R.; Cortadella, Jordi; Lavagno, Luciano; Lazarescu, Mihai T.
relevance_reason: Joint allocation of kernel compute units under shared resources/bandwidth; foundation for resource packing, not directive DSE.
research_problem: Choosing the number of compute units (CUs) per kernel and allocating them across multiple FPGAs to minimize the pipeline initiation interval of multi-kernel applications under per-FPGA resource and DRAM bandwidth constraints.
method: MINLP formulation minimizing alpha*II + beta*spreading subject to resource/bandwidth constraints; fast heuristic: relax to Geometric Programming (GPkit) for total CUs per kernel, branch-and-bound discretization, then greedy criticality-ordered allocation that consolidates CUs of a kernel on few FPGAs.
benchmark: AlexNet (16-bit fixed, 32-bit float), VGG16 (16-bit fixed) conv/pool/norm layers
hardware_platform: AWS F1 (8x Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs); optimizer on Intel Core i7-2600
metrics: Initiation interval, FPGA resource utilization (DSP/BRAM), spreading, optimizer CPU time
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: GP+A obtains results comparable to the MINLP solver but is 2-3 orders of magnitude faster (0.78 s to 4.4 s vs ~1 min to several hours).
limitations: Only linear pipelines; all communication via off-chip DRAM (no on-chip/FPGA-to-FPGA links); power not considered; kernel execution time assumed to scale linearly with CUs and independent of placement; VGG kernels not fully optimized; FC layers not implemented; end-to-end on-board runs of the allocated designs are not the main reported result.
gap_status: This paper does not report: adaptive evidence acquisition; lifecycle or configuration cost. Not a novelty claim.

title: Fast Energy-Optimal Multi-Kernel DNN-like Application Allocation on Multi-FPGA Platforms
authors: Shan, Junnan; Lazarescu, Mihai T.; Cortadella, Jordi; Lavagno, Luciano; Casu, Mario R.
relevance_reason: Energy-optimal joint multi-kernel allocation; foundation for packing and energy trade-offs.
research_problem: Finding minimum-power allocations of multi-kernel pipelined DNN-like applications on multi-FPGA platforms for a given throughput (II) constraint, fast enough to reprogram FPGAs at runtime as workloads change.
method: MINLP power model (static + dynamic, including DDR and PCIe transfer terms); heuristic H1 fixes F_min FPGAs and restricts each kernel to CU_min or CU_min+1 before MINLP; heuristic H2 exhaustively enumerates 2^K CU combinations with greedy allocation grouping kernels of similar execution time to lower frequency, picking minimum-power allocation.

method: Offline: LLVM-based source feature extraction and NSGA-II (pop 40, 24 generations) synthesis-based exploration of ~56 applications to build a knowledge base; hierarchical clustering of applications by code features and per-cluster Pareto-optimal directive distributions; online: assign directives to a new app from its cluster histograms with a probability threshold, re-proposing directives if the design is non-synthesizable/infeasible.

title: Stream-HLS: Towards Automatic Dataflow Acceleration
authors: Basalama, Suhail; Cong, Jason
relevance_reason: All kernels of a multi-kernel dataflow application scheduled jointly under a global budget; named in LITERATURE_STATUS_2026_09 as the neighbouring area our joint-evidence question must be distinguished from.
research_problem: HLS automation frameworks mostly insert pragmas without loop scheduling, target single kernels, lack global DSE, and miss graph-level pipelining (streaming) for multi-kernel applications.
method: MLIR-based framework: dataflow canonicalization and shared-buffer-to-FIFO conversion, an analytical performance model for dataflow designs with FIFO/shared-buffer communication, and MINLP (AMPL + Gurobi) global scheduling that jointly optimizes graph/node-level pipelining and node-level parallelization (Opt5); generates HLS and host code.
benchmark: 7 PolyBench kernels (e.g., 3mm, atax, bicg, gesummv), transformer multi-head self-attention and FFN, residual block, depthwise separable conv block, two MLPs, synthetic 7mm balanced/imbalanced
hardware_platform: AMD Alveo U280 (target; DSP limits 220, 2560 = ~1 SLR, 9024)
metrics: RTL-simulated cycle counts, speedup, DSE runtime, DSP utilization
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: Stream-HLS designs outperform prior automation frameworks and manually optimized abstraction-framework designs by up to 79.43x and 10.62x geometric means; combined MINLP (Opt5) achieves 27.67x-1300.42x speedups (geo-mean 314.89x) over the FIFO-only baseline; DSE runtime 176.41x faster than HIDA.

title: Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization
authors: Swersky, Kevin; Snoek, Jasper; Adams, Ryan P.
relevance_reason: Multi-task BO: methodological foundation for sharing evidence across benchmarks/tasks and cost-aware auxiliary tasks.
research_problem: Whether knowledge from previous or related hyperparameter optimizations can be transferred to new tasks to make Bayesian optimization faster (the cold-start problem), and how to exploit cheap related tasks.
method: Multi-task GP (intrinsic coregionalization, Kt kron Kx, slice-sampled) inside BO; (i) warm-start from completed related-task runs with EI, (ii) average-over-tasks objective choosing (x, task) by a two-step EI heuristic (fast k-fold CV), (iii) cost-sensitive multi-task entropy search maximizing information gain about the primary task's minimum per unit (GP-modeled log) cost.
benchmark: Shifted Branin-Hoo; logistic regression on MNIST (USPS as related task); CNN on SVHN (from CIFAR-10 / SVHN subset); CNN on k-means features for STL-10 (from CIFAR-10); PMF on MovieLens-100k (5-fold CV); online LDA on 200k-document corpus (50k-document subset as auxiliary)
metrics: Best (min) validation error / perplexity / RMSE vs function evaluations and vs time; average cumulative error (ACE); time to reach given error
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: multi-task BO 'significantly speeds up the optimization process when compared to the standard single-task approach'; e.g., MTBO reaches the LR minimum in ~40 min vs 100 min for STBO, and finds the online-LDA minimum in ~6 days vs 10 days (saving almost 4 days) by dynamically querying the cheaper task.
limitations: GP cost cubic in total observations across tasks; assumes positive task correlation (Cholesky elements sampled in log space); entropy-search acquisition evaluated over a fixed candidate set (top-C EI points); average-objective method uses a heuristic (impute then EI) rather than a principled criterion; single objective only.
gap_status: This paper does not report: decision or pareto stability. Not a novelty claim.

title: Constrained Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization through Optimistic Constraints Estimation
authors: Li, Diantong; Zhang, Fengxue; Liu, Chong; Chen, Yuxin
relevance_reason: Constrained multi-objective BO with feasibility estimation: foundation for feasibility-aware acquisition.
research_problem: Sample-efficient multi-objective BO when both objectives and constraints are unknown black-box functions, with theoretical guarantees that existing heuristic/approximate constrained MOBO methods lack.
method: COMBOO: restricts the search to the optimistic feasible region where all constraint UCBs exceed thresholds, and within it maximizes a random hypervolume scalarization of objective UCBs; can declare infeasibility; regret bounds on a constrained hypervolume + violation metric.
benchmark: Toy function (d=2,m=2,c=2); Branin-Currin (d=2,m=2,c=2); C2-DTLZ2 (d=4,m=2,c=1); Penicillin (d=7,m=3,c=3); Disc Brake Design (d=4,m=2,c=3); Caco-2++ (drug discovery, TDC); ESOL+
metrics: Simple/cumulative hypervolume regret, cumulative constraint violation, combined constraint regret C_t, observed best hypervolume
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: first constrained MOBO with guarantees similar to constrained single-objective algorithms (sample efficiency and infeasibility declaration); empirically COMBOO 'displayed a consistently strong performance, often aligning with the top-performing methods' and is comparable to all baselines in constraint regret on real-world problems.
limitations: Theory relies on discretized domain (claimed not fundamental); sequential q=1 comparison; qNEHVI converges faster on small-scale test functions; small problem dimensions for continuous cases.

title: Bayesian optimization of cooperative components for multi-stage aero-structural compressor blade design
authors: Pretsch, Lisa; Arsenyev, Ilya; Bartoli, Nathalie; Duddeck, Fabian

relevance_reason: All inter-kernel FIFO depths of a dataflow design sized jointly against whole-design latency; inter-kernel interaction boundary.
research_problem: Sizing FIFO channels in HLS dataflow designs trades latency (stalls/deadlock) against on-chip memory; static analyses cannot handle data-dependent control flow and co-simulation-based search is too slow.
method: Black-box multi-objective optimization with LightningSim incremental trace-based simulation (<1 ms per FIFO configuration) for latency and an analytical BRAM18K usage model; optimizers: random, grouped random, simulated annealing (weighted-sum sweep), grouped SA, greedy depth reduction; Pareto front extraction.
benchmark: 21-22 Stream-HLS dataflow kernels (linear algebra, DNN layers, e.g., k15mmtree, k15mmtseq, Autoencoder); FlowGNN PNA accelerator case study
metrics: Latency (cycles) relative to baselines, FIFO BRAM usage, Pareto frontiers, search runtime vs estimated co-simulation runtime
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: vs Baseline-Max, grouped optimizers find configurations with zero FIFO BRAMs and virtually no slowdown (1.0026x / 0.9994x latency); greedy saves 85.6% BRAM; vs Baseline-Min, grouped SA gives 0.52x latency with ~3.0 BRAMs and un-deadlocks designs; search is 10^5-10^7x faster than co-simulation-based search.
limitations: Optimizes for a single testbench input set; FIFOs mapped only to BRAM (no URAM), flip-flop overhead ignored; BRAM model targets UltraScale+.
gap_status: This paper does not report: staged evaluation; lifecycle or configuration cost. Not a novelty claim.

limitations: Stated: manually defined, small pattern library; simple estimator; templates focus on loop scheduling and bounded unrolling; only exhaustive-lite baseline (no BO/GA/prior DSE tools). Also: tiny kernels, HLS-estimate evaluation only, pattern assigned manually per kernel.

title: Fast and Accurate Estimation of Quality of Results in High-Level Synthesis with Machine Learning
authors: Dai, Steve; Zhou, Yuan; Zhang, Hang; Ustun, Ecenur; Young, Evangeline F.Y.; Zhang, Zhiru
relevance_reason: Estimates post-implementation QoR from HLS reports: cross-fidelity model.
research_problem: HLS-reported resource and timing estimates deviate strongly from post-implementation QoR (e.g., 125% LUT and 98% FF relative error), preventing meaningful DSE without running implementation.
method: Build a dataset of >1300 C-to-bitstream samples over 65 designs; extract 234 HLS-report features reduced to 87 via correlation filtering and L1 selection; train Lasso, ANN and XGBoost regression (LUT/FF/DSP/BRAM) and classification (timing met), single- and multi-task.

limitations: Requires running HLS to obtain features; dataset lacks directive variation (noted as future augmentation); random split rather than unseen-design evaluation; older 7-series devices.

title: FADO: Floorplan-Aware Directive Optimization for High-Level Synthesis Designs on Multi-Die FPGAs
authors: Du, Linfeng; Liang, Tingyuan; Sinha, Sharad; Xie, Zhiyao; Zhang, Wei
license_reported: no license stated for OA version (gold; https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3543622.3573188)
relevance_reason: Directives of multiple kernels co-optimized under shared per-die resources with floorplan interaction; joint multi-kernel boundary.
research_problem: HLS directive DSE for single-die FPGAs ignores per-die resource constraints and die-crossing delays on multi-die FPGAs, while global floorplanning per DSE step is too slow.
method: Formulates as multi-choice multi-dimensional bin-packing; iterative latency-bottleneck-guided greedy directive search with incremental floorplan legalization (worst-fit online packing, best-fit-decreasing offline re-packing, look-ahead/look-back) and incremental pipelining of die-crossing wires; function-level QoR library from HLS sampling.
benchmark: Six composite designs: CNN*2+2MM*1, MM*1+COV*2, MTTKRP*2+HEAT*2, MM*2+2MM*2, CNN*3+COV*2, MTTKRP*2+COV*2 (dataflow CNN/MM/MTTKRP from PolySA/AutoSA; 2MM/COV/HEAT from PolyBench)
hardware_platform: Xilinx Alveo U250 (floorplanning restricted to lower half, 4 slots on SLR0/SLR1; 65% per-slot resource limit)
metrics: DSE runtime, latency (cycles), Fmax, overall execution time, max resource utilization per slot
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: 693X-4925X shorter DSE runtime than DSE with global floorplanning, and 1.16X-8.78X improvement in overall workflow execution time after implementation on Alveo U250; 33.12% smaller latency on average vs iterative DO+AutoBridge FP, average Fmax 290.96 MHz.
limitations: Greedy bottleneck-driven, latency-oriented search (not full Pareto); evaluated on 6 synthesized composite benchmarks and restricted to half of U250; relies on per-function QoR library (template reuse); implementation non-determinism affects Fmax.

title: Automated Design Space Exploration in High-Level Physical Synthesis
authors: Du, Linfeng; Liang, Jiawei; Lau, Jason; Chi, Yuze; Xie, Yutong; Su, Chunyou; Ahmad, Afzal; He, Zifan; Ke, Jake; Ge, Jinming; Cong, Jason; Zhang, Wei; Guo, Licheng
relevance_reason: Metric-guided DSE over floorplan/implementation choices with post-route feedback: HLS-physical co-DSE foundation.
research_problem: High-Level Physical Synthesis (HLPS) QoR on multi-die FPGAs is unstable because many partitioning, floorplanning and pipelining parameters are chosen ad hoc; small parameter changes can change Fmax by 5x or cause routing failure.
method: Iterative, metric-guided DSE organized as a finite-state machine of six actions; after each place-and-route, extracts physical metrics (per-slot utilization, congestion windows, critical-path distribution, slot-crossing distribution, vacant zones) via RapidWright and Vivado Tcl and applies heuristics (e.g., slot-wise limit and wire-capacity adjustment algorithms) plus ILP floorplanning/routing.
benchmark: Sextans (SpMM), Callipepla (CG solver), MM 10x13 systolic array, Serpens (SpMV), NTT, GPT-2 Medium accelerator
hardware_platform: AMD Alveo U55C, U280, U250, Versal VHK158 (implementation only; AMD EPYC 7742 server)
metrics: Post-route Fmax (MHz), cumulative DSE time (hours), number of solutions and parallel batches, resource utilization per slot
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: average frequency of 311.06 MHz, 2.42x the Vitis/Vivado toolchain (128.48 MHz) and 1.67x AutoBridge (186.21 MHz).
limitations: Heuristic sequential action order without optimality guarantee; single PnR iteration can exceed ten hours so DSE takes days (e.g., up to 325 h cumulative) with limited coverage; design-level HLS partitioning issues (e.g., NTT large module) cannot be fixed by HLPS parameters.

title: FOS: A Modular FPGA Operating System for Dynamic Workloads
authors: Vaishnav, Anuj; Pham, Khoa Dang; Powell, Joseph; Koch, Dirk
relevance_reason: PR-based FPGA OS measuring swap/update latency and switching HLS variants at runtime.
research_problem: FPGA systems lack modularity and multi-tenancy support; component dependencies force whole-stack recompilation, and static accelerator allocation under-utilizes resources for dynamic workloads.
method: Modular development flow (shell, accelerators, drivers, runtime compiled in isolation with fixed interfaces), relocatable PR regions with bitstream manipulation (BitMan), JSON descriptors, and a resource-elastic scheduler arbitrating PR regions in time and space and reusing already-loaded accelerators.
benchmark: Spector benchmark suite (OpenCL/HLS), AES, Normal Estimation, Black-Scholes, Mandelbrot, Sobel
hardware_platform: Xilinx ZCU102, UltraZed, Ultra-96 (Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC)
metrics: Compilation (P&R + bitstream) time, component update latency, memory bandwidth, execution latency/speedup
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: 'FOS can speed up the compilation time by up to 2.34x and avoid standard recompilation requirements to reduce the update latencies by over 100x'; accelerator swap latency 3.81 ms (Ultra-96) / 6.77 ms (ZCU102); DCT achieved 3.55x for 2x resources by switching to a larger implementation.
limitations: Requires homogeneous PR regions and fixed interfaces; memory bandwidth contention (row-buffer pollution) limits scaling; rapid multi-tenant requests induce reconfiguration latencies; evaluated on embedded MPSoC boards only.

title: PLD: Fast FPGA Compilation to Make Reconfigurable Acceleration Compatible with Modern Incremental Refinement Software Development
authors: Xiao, Yuanlong; Micallef, Eric; Butt, Andrew; Hofmann, Matthew; Alston, Marc; Goldsmith, Matthew; Merczynski-Hait, Andrew; DeHon, André
relevance_reason: DFX-based fast compilation trading compile cost against QoR: build/configuration cost source.
research_problem: FPGA compile times of hours inhibit incremental edit-compile-debug refinement; the paper introduces separate compilation and linking of HLS operators using DFX partial-reconfiguration pages to offer compile-time/performance trade-off levels.
method: Partition the FPGA into DFX pages with a packet-switched linking network (BFT); compile each operator separately with Vitis HLS + Vivado using abstract shell; load partial bitstreams and configure links at runtime; same C source can target RISC-V soft cores.
benchmark: Rosetta benchmark suite (3D Rendering, Digit Recognition, Spam Filter, Optical Flow, BNN, Face Detection)
metrics: Compile time (per stage and total), application runtime/throughput, clock frequency, resource utilization
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: separate compilation (-O1) reduces compile times from 1-2 hours to 10-20 minutes (4.2-7.3x speedup) and -O0 to under 4 seconds; -O1 designs run 1.5-10x slower than monolithic, while -O3 decomposed designs match monolithic performance.
limitations: -O1 performance limited by linking-network bandwidth and overlay overhead; requires streaming-dataflow operator decomposition (hls::stream interfaces); increased BRAM use for FIFOs; page sizes fixed.

title: Power Consumption Model for Partial and Dynamic Reconfiguration

title: CORDOBA: Carbon-Efficient Optimization Framework for Computing Systems
